sentence_of_record: ESCALATE-LLAMA-LAW (2026-09-16, 666 calls): FRAMEWORK item 24: FAIL, as predicted (JUDGE-2x2); escalation does not buy back the model-anchored residue. The reasoning judge's gain on these cells is a TIE-REMOVAL gain, not an accuracy-on-committed gain (treatment B +0.000), and it is LARGER on the control model than on Llama-3.1-70B, the model the residue is anchored to: the four established wrong-direction edges of KEY-TIE-DECLINE's composed rule are not what a stronger judge fixes. A model-anchored escalation rule at 10 cce per match is NOT adopted; the framework's fallback for that residue stays 'unseparated, not certified'. The J1-R rubric's p8a29 contamination favours J1-R, so the FAIL stands a fortiori on the clean stratum. plain_description.what: Re-judges every Law and Philosophy match of Llama-3.1-70B, plus a matched control model (Qwen1.5-72B), with a stronger reasoning judge. It then compares the verdicts with the cheap judge on the same matches (666 calls).
plain_description.why: A few remaining wrong-direction verdicts were tied to Llama-3.1-70B in those cells. The test asks whether escalating to a stronger judge just there fixes them.
plain_description.information: A gain on the treated model and none on the control would justify a targeted escalation rule. Result: done, failed as predicted. The stronger judge mostly removes ties. It does not make committed verdicts more accurate (gain +0.000 on the treated model), and its gain is larger on the control. The escalation rule is not adopted, and these cells stay 'unseparated, not certified'. The comparison was against a proxy of the shipped judge, and the script was edited during the run window. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
